citation.title: Shell disc beads and the development of class-based society at the K2-Mapungubwe settlement complex (South Africa)

license.notes: Check figure, image, and third-party material credit lines individually before reusing assets.

snapshot.reason: Publisher article and abstract reviewed; no complete source snapshot or bead-level table has been ingested.

reported_claims.statement: The study analysed 6,172 shell disc beads from phases II-IV and from higher-status and lower-status areas of the K2-Mapungubwe settlement complex.
reported_claims.source_locator: section: The K2-Mapungubwe shell disc bead sample
sampling_limitations_reported_by_source: Only excavated material retaining site, context, or other provenience information was sampled.
Provenience information was often lacking for much of the early excavation material.
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: The paper reports its analysed sample and sample-selection rule; the sample is not a census of all beads or all past activity.

reported_claims.statement: The paper reports temporal and spatial differences in bead assemblages, including a greater prevalence of Achatina beads in earlier phases and ostrich eggshell bead dominance after approximately AD 1220.
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: Assemblage pattern and the authors' interpretation; not direct proof of a particular trade route, institution, or individual status.

source_family.notes: Excavation contexts cite earlier work by Eloff, Meyer, Jones and others. Preserve those source lineages before treating this analysis as independent evidence for the same contexts.

citation.title: A Bayesian chronology for Great Zimbabwe: re-threading the sequence of a vandalised monument

license.notes: Metadata and abstract only; obtain permission or use licensed data for full text, tables, and figures.

snapshot.reason: Publisher abstract and metadata reviewed; radiocarbon observations, stratigraphic relations, imports, priors, and posterior outputs have not been ingested.

reported_claims.statement: The study combines available radiocarbon dates with limited stratigraphic information and datable imports into a Bayesian chronology.

The authors place the likely start of Great Zimbabwe stone-wall construction around the end of the 12th or beginning of the 13th century, with a peak in the 14th and 15th centuries, and conclude that Great Zimbabwe occupation overlapped with Mapungubwe.
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: A published probabilistic chronology and interpretation; do not convert broad intervals into exact year-level facts or a universal successor relation.

source_family.notes: The analysis reuses earlier radiocarbon, stratigraphic, and imported-object evidence. Resolve shared contexts and dating datasets before cross-paper evidence aggregation.

citation.author: Tim Forssman
citation.title: Contesting space: contact between foragers and farmers in the Mapungubwe cultural landscape, South Africa

license.notes: Metadata and article page reviewed; check publisher terms before redistributing content or images.

snapshot.reason: Article page and reported survey summary reviewed; site-level lithic records and dated contexts have not been ingested.

reported_claims.statement: The article reports a survey over approximately 160 square kilometres and identifies two broad lithic assemblage types, with possible interaction between foragers and farming communities.
uncertainties: temporal relationship between some assemblage types is unresolved
the interpretation that toolkit differences reflect interaction is presented as possible, not certain
the article reports foragers disappearing from the archaeological record around the end of the Mapungubwe phase; this is not evidence of population extinction
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: A survey and interpretation of lithic assemblages; not proof that a living population disappeared or was assimilated.

source_family.notes: The article discusses and cites Van Doornum's earlier survey and chronology work. Preserve those source relationships.

citation.title: Archaeological science and globalisation: Great Zimbabwe

license.notes: This is a project summary, not a substitute for the underlying archaeometallurgical publications or artifact datasets.

snapshot.reason: Project summary reviewed; crucible and metal-object measurements have not been ingested.

reported_claims.statement: The project describes Great Zimbabwe as connected directly and indirectly with Indian Ocean Rim regions, with gold, iron, ivory and other commodities supplied outward and tin bronzes, brasses, glass beads and ceramics received.
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: A research-project summary of exchange and archaeometallurgical questions; not direct proof that a specific artifact followed a direct route or that two named actors traded directly.

source_family.notes: Underlying archaeometallurgical publications, excavations, object contexts, and material-provenance analyses must be located and linked before quantitative exchange-network modelling.

citation.title: Implications of new AMS dates for the Khami Period in the Mapungubwe Landscape

license.notes: Verify article license and access rights for any extracted tables or underlying dating records.

snapshot.reason: Publisher abstract and article metadata reviewed; dated contexts, measurements, and calibration output have not been ingested.

reported_claims.statement: The article describes post-Mapungubwe reoccupation of the Limpopo Valley first by Sotho communities associated with Icon pottery, followed by Kalanga speakers associated with Khami pottery.
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: A published regional sequence interpretation; not a complete demographic history or proof that every site followed the same sequence.

reported_claims.statement: The authors describe Sotho and Kalanga occupations as occurring in pulses during higher-rainfall periods, and place the senior Kalanga chief at Machemma about 60 km south while petty chiefs administered parts of the valley.
alternative_explanations_to_preserve: rainfall variability as one factor among several
political organization inferred from settlement and pottery patterns
chronological uncertainty in the AMS and ceramic sequence
reported_claims.claim_ceiling: The article's interpretation of a regional sequence; not a measured continuous population curve or a fully resolved political map.

source_family.notes: Same authors and overlapping regional chronology research as HIST001-SRC-AMS-2021. Treat as related evidence until sample-level overlap and source lineage have been checked.
